facts.text: Sewickley Heights was incorporated as a borough in 1935 after the Allegheny Country Club moved there in 1902, sparking wealthy settlement.
The borough’s historic district status protects many early 20‑century estates, making it the only Pennsylvania borough entirely designated as an historic district.
A 33‑acre site hosts both the Fern Hollow Nature Center and the Sewickley Heights History Center, preserving local heritage and natural beauty.
The History Center’s collection includes antique carriages, vintage attire, and a film archive that honors Pittsburgh industrialists’ lifestyles.
Oil and gas wells discovered in the 1880s still dot the Heights, remnants of an early industrial boom.
The Sewickley Heights Borough Park, formed from donated land in the 1960s and 1970s, now covers about 600 acres of hiking and horse‑riding trails.
